A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of calcium salts in the enrichment of soy yogurt is a promising alternative to the traditional calcium enrichment of dairy yogurt, because the soy yogurt enriched with calcium salts presented calcium contents equivalent to or superior to those found in traditional yogurt, and the technological properties (time for fermentation, pH, titrable acidity, viscosity, consistency and calcium content) and sensory properties (acceptance and preference) of the product were adequate.

the addition of calcium salts in the form of citrate, phosphate, carbonate, glyconate and lactate to soya yogurt, in the concentration of 600 mg of elemental calcium per liter of product, did not cause any undesirable sensorial changes, and the fermentation time did not exceed those found in conventional industrial processes, and therefore all salts tested were viable for the enrichment of soya yogurt with calcium.
the addition of calcium salts in a concentration of 600mg of Ca/l to soya yogurt did not alter the technological and sensory properties of the product.
